title: Peri Peri Chicken
subtitle: Spicy marinated chicken thighs roasted at high heat
excerpt: A blended red chilli, garlic, and smoked paprika marinade that chars beautifully in a hot oven. The longer the chicken marinates, the deeper the heat goes into the meat.
sourceNotes: Peri peri is a Portuguese-African chilli preparation popularised as a marinade for chicken across southern Africa and Portugal.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze marinated raw chicken for up to 3 months. Defrost fully before roasting.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate overnight for the most intense flavour.

content.text: Score the chicken thighs before marinating so the peri peri sauce gets right into the meat. Blend the marinade until smooth.

items.prepNote: skin-on if possible, scored a few times
roughly chopped; deseed for less heat

content.text: Blend the chillies, garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, smoked paprika, sweet paprika, oregano, olive oil, and red wine vinegar until smooth. Season well.
Score the chicken thighs 2 or 3 times through to the bone. Pour the marinade over the chicken and toss to coat. Cover and chill for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 220 degrees C. Arrange the chicken in a single layer in a roasting tin, skin side up.
Roast for 28 to 30 minutes until the skin is charred in places and the juices run clear.
Serve with chips, rice, or flatbread and a simple salad.

items.symptom: Marinade burnt before the chicken cooked through.
items.cause: Oven too hot or thighs were very thick.
items.fix: Cover with foil after 15 minutes; remove for the last 5 to char.

items.symptom: Chicken not very spicy despite 4 chillies.
items.cause: Seeds removed or chillies were mild variety.
items.fix: Leave some seeds in or use hotter varieties next time.

items.cause: Too much marinade left on or pieces were wet going in.
items.fix: Shake off excess marinade and pat skin dry before roasting.
